body:
`check` and `test` work on Rust projects, ready for task:ba1542d1a967b9b7 to check every submit (D-158 point 3). Plan: this task's investigation, note 8.

- `check` runs `cargo check --all-targets --message-format=json --offline`, one `target/` per project, warmed at import without making import wait. Measured on `solace-cli/`: 0.71 s warm after a one-function edit, 10.4 s cold.
- Map each error's primary span to its symbol with `FileMap` / `locate`; follow `expansion` back to the macro call site. An error reported once per target is shown once.
- Borrow errors only appear once type errors are fixed, so a fix can take a second round; the reply says so.
- `cargo::format_item` formats one item with rustfmt and the project's `rustfmt.toml` (methods wrapped in `impl _ { … }`); never a whole file, since the crate isn't rustfmt-clean (D-158 point 5). Used by the submit task.
- `test` runs `cargo test` (26–28 s) and reads failures by libtest name (`board::tests::x`).
- A machine without `cargo`: the project's lane on the board shows "Needs the Rust toolchain (`cargo`)" (a `needs` flag in `/projects`, drawn in `solace-cli/board`), reads still work, and `submit`/`check`/`test` are refused with that message.
- Until task:ba1542d1a967b9b7 lands, `submit` to a Rust project replies "Rust projects can't take `submit` yet".
- An undo (`board.rs::revert`) in a Rust project is checked too.

Out of scope: Rust `submit` (task:ba1542d1a967b9b7), the bubblewrap sandbox (task:7db8dd126a22c863), cargo's suggested fixes, refs and test reach.
title: Rust: check, test and missing cargo
